findings.title: Opaque JSON objects with serde private Number keys are silently changed into numbers

trigger.input: Valid selected Package envelope with data.vendor={"$serde_json::private::Number":"123"}; the reserved name is literal application JSON, not serde internal data.

findings.expected: The vendor field remains an object with that exact member, or admission explicitly refuses; it must not silently become numeric data.
findings.actual: Direct Value deserialization with arbitrary_precision recognizes the first private key and creates Value::Number(123). Root observed actual_vendor=123 and preserved_object=false.
findings.why_existing_tests_missed: model.rs exact-value fixtures parse expected JSON through the same serde Value path. Existing opaque/large-number tests use ordinary keys and cannot expose common-mode private-key reinterpretation.
findings.runtime_scope: Root executed an immutable exported F33/F34 dependency copy sharing this exact Document::from_json boundary; this reviewer did not execute anything and does not claim a separate build of component #8.

dependency_evidence.meaning: ValueVisitor/KeyClassifier recognizes Number and, when enabled, RawValue marker keys.

plan_action.avoid_duplicate: Parser/interchange reviewer cross-references this cause for F33 and C03b/C03c; do not create a separate global repair per downstream PR.

findings.title: Legacy ResourceSet name resolution has no bound on flat conjugation reference chains

trigger.input: One flat admitted document with arbitrarily many ConjugatedPortDefinition roots; each owns a PortConjugation whose originalPortDefinition references the next root, ending in an ordinary named PortDefinition. Raw JSON nesting stays shallow.
trigger.operation: ResourceSet::effective_name(...Name,SemanticElementIds), or qualified-root lookup which asks is_unnamed.

findings.expected: An explicit bounded failure/cancellation or iterative traversal; no process-stack dependence for admitted reference graphs.
findings.actual: name_inner recursively follows each acyclic reference with only a seen-set cycle check. F46 has a separate 128-step iterative bound, which does not change this legacy path.
findings.why_existing_tests_missed: Cycle and small naming examples do not exercise long acyclic cross-reference chains; JSON-depth tests cannot bound a flat reference graph.
findings.not_observed: No crash, timing or threshold was executed by this reviewer.

findings.title: Graph indexes recursively duplicate subtrees and peer counts rescan the full node map

trigger.input: Wide namespaces with K Memberships and N objects, plus deep containment and realistic large leaf bodies.
trigger.operation: Initialize a new element / ask exact-class peer count / build F46 naming snapshots.

findings.expected: Measured bounded interactive behavior and snapshot memory, with responsive cancellation and no avoidable repeated full-subtree retention.
findings.actual: Each Index node stores a clone of its complete data subtree; nested data are copied repeatedly. Peer-count implementation performs a full node-map scan for every membership (O(K*N)). NativeContext replays/clones the document and builds indexes again per query prefix. F46 additionally owns several document/index copies.
findings.why_existing_tests_missed: Small synthetic fixtures establish ordering and failure atomicity but do not measure wide/deep scaling, allocation, or cancellation latency.
findings.not_observed: No numeric latency/RSS regression is asserted; actual benchmarks are required before optimizing.

findings.title: Local editor history retains an unbounded full document per committed edit

trigger.input: A realistically large document followed by many scalar/name commits.
trigger.operation: Editor::begin, Transaction::apply, commit, and undo/redo from the actual UI.

findings.expected: A measured retention/budget policy and responsive undo/redo; failed/cancelled edits remain atomic.
findings.actual: begin clones base/staged snapshots, apply clones the staged document, and each successful commit appends a full prior Document to an uncapped Vec. Retained history scales with edits times document size.
findings.why_existing_tests_missed: Atomicity/undo tests use small fixtures and a few edits; storage byte-budget fixes do not bound this in-memory Editor history.

findings.title: F47 serializes and reparses the full document before rejecting unrelated oversized opaque data

trigger.input: Source empty/finite and a valid Document with few or zero model nodes but a large wide/deep opaque envelope payload.
trigger.operation: validate with an explicit rule selection.

findings.expected: Bound/inspect the existing admitted document without creating an unbounded pretty JSON copy and another DOM before shape/rule admission.
findings.actual: 2048 model-row bound is followed by document.to_json() (pretty serialization) and serde_json::from_str of the full result. Model count does not bound opaque payload size or pretty indentation amplification.

findings.title: Name conversion output loops only poll cancellation at their endpoints

trigger.input: Caller selects a large UTF16-unit allowance and supplies a long quoted/escaped name.
trigger.operation: sanitize_name or unsanitize_name while another thread requests cancellation.

findings.expected: Documented bounded cancellation latency across every long conversion pass.
findings.actual: units() polls periodically, but sanitation/escaping loops and the simple-name all() scan have only before/after cancellation checks. Numeric parsing is documented nonpreemptible; these extra loops lack an equivalent explicit bound/policy.

gates: Mid-loop cancellation on ordinary and escape-expanding names
